entries.title: Proverbs 26:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: By flying - Secures itself from the fowler. Not come - Upon the innocent person, but he shall escape from it like a bird.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: According - So as to imitate his folly, by passionate or reproachful speeches.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: According - So as his folly needs and requires, convincing him strongly, reproving him sharply, and exposing him to just shame.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Cutteth off the feet - Of his messenger; bids one go that wants legs. Drinketh - Drinking, in scripture, frequently denotes the plentiful doing or receiving of any thing.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The legs - Heb. the legs of the lame are lifted up, in going, or in dancing, which is done with great inequality and uncomeliness. So - No less incident are wise and pious speeches from a foolish and ungodly man.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:8
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bindeth - Whereby he hinders his own design of throwing the stone out of it. So - No less absurd is he that giveth to a fool that honour which he is not capable of using aright.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:9
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A thorn - As a thorn is in a drunkard's hand, which he cannot manage cautiously, but employs to his own and others hurt. So - As unprofitable, and, by accident, hurtful to himself and others.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rewardeth - Will certainly give that recompence which is deserved by fools and transgressors, by such as sin either thro' ignorance, or wilfully.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Turneth - Moving hither and thither upon it, but not removing from its place.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A reason - A satisfactory reason of ail their actions.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: He - Who is going upon the way. With strife - In which he is not concerned, nor any way obliged to meddle. That taketh - Exposes himself to needless hazard.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Burning - With malice or hatred: A slanderous or evil tongue. Dross - Such a tongue and heart are of no real worth, although sometimes they make a shew of it, as dross does of silver.

entries.title: Proverbs 26:27
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rolleth - Up the hill with design to do mischief to some person.
